title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
prompt:
Read a temperature in degrees Celsius with `input()` (it can have decimals), convert it with `celsius * 9 / 5 + 32`, and print only the Fahrenheit number.

For example, if the input is `20`, the program prints:

```
68.0
```
starter: # read the temperature, convert it, print the result
hints: `input()` always returns a string. Convert it to a number before calculating.
Use `float()` so that decimals such as `37.5` work.
`celsius = float(input())`, then calculate and `print` the result.

title: Next birthday
prompt:
Read a name and then an age, each on its own line, with `input()`. Print one line saying how old the person will be next year.

For example, with the input `Maya` and `29`, the program prints:

```
Maya will be 30 next year
```
starter: # read the name, read the age, print the sentence
solution:
name = input()
age = int(input())
print(name, "will be", age + 1, "next year")
hints: Two `input()` calls: the first line is the name, the second the age. Only the age needs converting.
`age = int(input())`, then you can add 1 to it.
